mustKnow.item: The tape on 9/28: indices closed lower, driven by US-Iran headlines. Trump rejected a ceasefire (WSJ); later reports of talks, possible sanctions relief and Iran agreeing to halt enrichment sent oil sharply lower
mustKnow.note: Ours k10 covers it. LeapEdge has one generic line.

mustKnow.item: Oil supply: Saudi east-west pipeline repaired; Aramco weighing about a $9/bbl OSP cut for Gulf of Oman loadings (the premium had been $10-20); US diesel up 70%+ since the conflict; European pump price 1.85 to about 2.2 EUR/L
mustKnow.note: Ours has the OSP cut but no diesel +70%.

mustKnow.item: Rates: the 10Y hit 5.274% intraday; risk premium at a 5-month high; no cuts priced before mid-2028. The creator thinks the selloff is overdone (Lagarde dovish, ECB October hike <40%). 5.3% may be a phased top; above it, 5.5%
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge makes the 5-month high the yield's, and omits Lagarde/ECB.

mustKnow.item: Gold plunged (strong USD, higher yields). BTC is range-bound: short-term pullback pressure, medium-term support intact

S&P 500: lost its 5-day MA, held its monthly MA. Retail net buying at a 2-year low (Vanda). GS: breadth narrowest since dot-com, median stock 16% below its 52-week high, under half above their 200-day. GS sentiment -0.9 (equal to the March low), historically +0.5% the next month. New highs are possible once yields fall, if rates stop rising
mustKnow.note: Both omit the -16% median and the 200-day statistic.

mustKnow.item: Midterms: options imply only about 0.8% after the Nov 4 vote (similar to an FOMC day). JPM warns of upside risk that volatility mean-reverts, with October typically the peak

Semis: SOX -1.6%, ARM -8.7%, QCOM -7%+, INTC -5.7% after OpenAI paused training of its most advanced model. Selling is profit-taking, not shorting. Direction awaits Micron earnings on Wednesday. SK Hynix spin-off worries are noise

NVDA: up against the market (with a long upper shadow). Buyback raised by $150B to $235B remaining, to be completed by the end of FY2028. Forward P/E under 17x, a decade low and half of last year: 'no wonder it won't fall'
mustKnow.note: Neither gives the $235B total or the FY2028 completion.

mustKnow.item: META: back at its 10-day MA. The bull trend is intact above it; below it, beware a reversal. OpenAI's always-on assistant 'O' at DevDay 9/29 is a competitive risk
MDB: -27% intraday, -18.5% close after the CEO left for Meta. $300 is the medium-term bull/bear line: holding it could make a phased bottom, losing it opens $270 or lower

Regional banks: Apollo warns AI agents will move deposits to high-yield accounts (checking 0.01%, savings 0.04%). The creator's personal advice is to keep deposits at large systemically important banks (BAC, WFC) and avoid small banks
mustKnow.note: Only in ours' tickerSentiment, where the deposit advice is misread as bullish BAC/WFC stock views. LeapEdge has a generic keyPoint.

mustKnow.item: SpaceX: Starship reached orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, but the stock slipped below its short-term MAs. A 1.3B-share lockup expiry in early November with Q3 results is the key near-term catalyst
TSLA: about -4%; JPM and GS cut Q3 delivery estimates; fuel-efficiency rules loosened. Losing the 50-day MA would trigger a new pullback

BA: at a 6-month low; 737 MAX software fault, FAA scrutiny, United and Southwest refusing aircraft, 777X delays hurting cash flow. Likely to retest the 200/250-month MA zone. If you want to bottom-fish, scale in slowly
mustKnow.note: Ours k19 drops the retest expectation and the scale-in advice.

sentimentIssues: Every one of 29 rows has ticker null, including 'ARM', which is spoken as a ticker.
BAC and WFC bullish is a misclassification of deposit-safety advice (see fidelityErrors).
NVDA is split across 英伟达 and 英偉達 with different stances (neutral vs long). 'Long' overstates the creator's view, which is observational.
MDB (3 rows), META (2), TSLA (2) and S&P 500 (3) are duplicated. 美股三大股指 and 美债 are non-instrument rows.
BA bearish/conditional, META conditional, TSLA bearish/watch and SK Hynix neutral ('noise') are all correct in direction.
why: Ours failed before producing a brief or calls (a fix is pending), so a PM gets 19 keyPoints (4 duplicates) and 29 unresolved sentiment rows with no ticker. The keyPoints are more complete and more accurate than LeapEdge's: they include oil, gold, BTC, semis, SpaceX and the ECB. LeapEdge delivers 5 usable trade cards with tickers and levels, but 2 of 5 are overstated or false (NVDA, BA), and MDB's entry/target/stop is incoherent. On this run LeapEdge is more usable. Once the fix lands, ours should win if it emits conditional calls with support/resistance roles.
recommendations: Fix the translation-step failure. It should also degrade gracefully: if translation fails, still publish calls and the brief in the source language instead of failing the whole run.

For daily market-wrap videos, allow 'conditional' technical calls with level roles taken from the quote: MDB {kind:'support', value_original:'300美元'}, {kind:'downside_target_if_broken', value_original:'270美元'}. Never map them to entry/target/stop, which is LeapEdge's MDB error.
Normalize Traditional to Simplified Chinese (e.g. OpenCC) before ticker resolution and dedup. 英偉達 and 英伟达 must be one instrument.

Classify advice type: personal-finance or banking advice ('开在大银行') is not an equity stance. Add adviceType: investment | personal_finance | illustrative, and exclude non-investment types from tickerSentiment.

Ask the extraction prompt for creator forward views on each named stock ('大概率将会再次向下测试200月与250月均线', '有进一步走低的风险'). Ours k19 and k18 recorded the news but dropped the forward view, which is the actionable part.
